lectures.title: How to measure Recursive Algorithms that make multiple calls?

cues.en: All right.
In the previous lecture we have looked at how to measure recursive algorithm, and we have said that
the time complexity for that function is on.
Now in this lecture we will look at tricky recursive call which calls itself twice.
So here we have a function which takes an integer as a parameter.
And in the first condition we check if n is less or equal to one, then we return one.
Otherwise we call this function with n minus one twice and summing up their values.
This function is similar to the function that we discussed in the previous lecture.
The difference is that here the function calls itself twice.
Many people might think that if in case of previous function, the time complexity is o n, where the
function calls itself once.
So here calling itself twice can be o n squared time complexity, but this assumption is completely
incorrect.
Rather than making assumptions, let's drive the runtime by walking through the code.
Suppose we call this function for the parameter of n4.
So in this case, when we call it for n4, it's going to call itself twice with n3.
And n3 will call itself twice with n2.
And this answer also will call itself twice with n2.
And this n2 also will call itself twice.
For n is equal to one.
And here again for n is equal to one.
And it continues like this.
Now how many times the function calls itself with the parameter of four.
Here you don't need to count it.
The number of the calls is 15.
So what does this number tells us.
So if you look at over here, we can easily see that the depth of this structure is going to be four.
Which means that for a function with the n parameter the depth will be n.
And if you look at each level over here, we can see that in zeroth level we have only one function
call.
In the first level we have two function call.
In the second level we have four function call, and in the third level we have eight function call.
So which means that we can express each level with the level to the power of two.
So here in the level zero we have two to the power of zero which is going to be one.
Then in level two as we said we have two calls.
We can write it two to the power of one, which is going to be two.
Then in the second level we have four function calls.
We can write it two to the power of two, which is going to be four.
And in the third level we have eight function call.
We can call it two to the power of three which is going to be eight.
Now if we sum up them together it's going to be something like this.
So this is a question that comes from math.
If you write two to the power of zero plus two to the power of one and continues two to the power of
n is it's going to be equal two to the power of n plus one minus one.
So in this case if you calculate it for four it's going to be 16 minus one which is going to be 15.
So if you count this it's going to be 15 number of calls.
So from here if we just eliminate the constant term, we can say that the time complexity for this function
is going to be two to the power of n.
So we can easily write the equation like this.
Or branches with the power of depth.
So branch over here is that we are calling the function two times.
So every time when we are calling the function it's dividing into the two branches.
So we are writing the branch and as a parameter which we are passing in which is going to be the depth
of this structure.
And that's why we are going to put it like this.
Now when it comes to the Fibonacci function here again, you see that in case of Fibonacci we are calling
the Fibonacci function twice.
That's why the number of the branches is going to be two.
And the depth is going to be n, which is the n parameter that we are passing over here.
That's why the time complexity is going to be two to the power of n.
Similarly, the space complexity is going to be o n because here when we are calling the Fibonacci function,
the function calls will be inserted in the stack memory.
That's why in the worst case it's going to take on space complexity.
So hopefully everything is clear us.
